Power-Systems Engineer said about it: I read the Dynamic braking - Wikipedia (E61) which states dynamic braking is use of a traction motor as a generator when slowing, termed rheostatic if dissipated as heat in brake grid resistors with thermal monitoring to protect resistors, which maps to the outrunner onto the 4 ohm dump plus the spring disc sized by the dynamic-brake-stop-sizing skill (E59); I read the How to Short a DC Motor: Short-Circuit (Dynamic) Braking Explained (2026) (E62) which states short-circuit braking torque decays to zero when the shaft stops, and I confirm what Safety-Control Integrator takes from the Braking ideas for wind turbines (E42) that brakes are spring-applied fail-safe, which from my side means electrics alone cannot park because the electrical-only runaway check (E48) with 0.155 N·m electrical against 0.480 N·m wind torque fails at 9.12e+03 Revolutions Per Minute (RPM), meaning shaft turns per minute.
Safety-Control Integrator said about it: For the Manager, sensing gets a distant-field second means in the elevator-chain analogy sense (C27) and I confirm what Power-Systems Engineer takes from the How to Short a DC Motor: Short-Circuit (Dynamic) Braking Explained (2026) (E62) that short-circuit braking torque falls to zero at zero speed, which from my side means electrics can help slow but only spring friction can park.
Safety-Control Integrator said about it: For Power-Systems Engineer, I confirm what you take from the How to Short a DC Motor: Short-Circuit (Dynamic) Braking Explained (2026) (E62) that short-circuit torque falls to zero at zero speed, which from shutdown side means electrics can help slow but only spring friction can keep the rotor parked.
